description: Revocation closure `retraction-after-correction` over the 28-entry toy corpus (core spec §5.1, §5.3), evaluated at the checkpoint committing the trigger.
note: Record A was corrected twice earlier in the corpus — to A2 at entry 6 and to A3 (hmac-sha256:8d8bdbc4e812ae6c4646aadc00dae223343e13c7f080ce56f4a6d1663039aba7) at entry 12 — and is now RETRACTED outright at entry 18. Core spec §5.1: "For a retraction on (ds, X), the seed set is exactly {(ds, X)} — retractions never seed superseded replacements." So the seeds are {A} alone, and the consumers of A2 — S1' (sha256:e5f83af3b1fc03898a1c31871a12b82bce702f41b27abb182fda0de1d9e7dba7) at entry 7 and W1/W2 at entry 10 — are NOT affected. Retracting A says nothing about A2: A2 is a separately introduced record with its own history. Contrast `supersession-chain`, where a *correction* of the same original does seed A2, because that correction supersedes the one that produced it.
